title: A child is born
hookLine: Guru Arjan's joy at the birth of his son Hargobind (Asa M5, ang 396)

cards: The text arrives at 4:12 in the morning: a photo of a tiny, furious, red-faced person in a striped hospital blanket. Name to follow. Everyone's fine.
Suddenly the whole family group chat is awake, typing in capital letters. Some joy can't wait for a polite hour.
Tradition says Guru Arjan knew that kind of joy in a village near Amritsar, when his wife, Mata Ganga, gave birth to a son after long waiting. And his answer to that joy was a song.

teach.h: THE TRUE GURU HAS SENT THIS CHILD.
teach.b: The shabad is in Raag Asa, on ang 396. It begins, in effect: the True Guru has sent this child. The long-lived one has been born, by destiny.

teach.h: A MOTHER'S HEART FULL OF DELIGHT.
teach.b: He came to dwell in the womb, and his mother's heart is full of delight. Then the refrain: a son is born, a devotee of the Lord; what was written from the beginning is now revealed to all.
And then: in the tenth month, by the Lord's command, the child was born. Sorrow is gone, great joy has come, and the companions sing the Guru's hymns in delight.

The child was Hargobind, who would become the sixth Guru. Some hear a gentle play in the refrain: bhagat govind, a devotee of Govind, the Lord, and the boy named Hargobind. Notice where the credit goes.
The child is a gift, sent. The joy is real and physical, a mother's delight, a household singing, but the first line points past the parents to the Giver.
Sikh families sing this shabad at births, and bring a newborn to the gurdwara for an Ardas of thanks. And because the hymn says son, a fair note: Gurbani gives a daughter no lesser place.
Guru Nanak asked, in Asa di Var, why anyone would speak ill of woman, from whom kings are born.

teach.h: DAUGHTERS WELCOMED WITH THE SAME JOY.
teach.b: Families sing this same shabad for a girl too.
A child is a gift arriving, whoever the child is.

how: Sikh families sing Guru Arjan's 'satgur saachai deeaa bhej' at the birth of a child, and bring the newborn to the gurdwara for an Ardas of thanks and the naming ceremony.

practice: Bring to mind a new parent you know, a child recently born in your circle, or someone expecting, and if no one comes, remember a baby you once held.

Picture the child's face and the parents' tired, astonished eyes, and let yourself feel glad for them, without any if or but. If you pray, you can thank the One for the gift, or ask a long life for the child with a quiet Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Hargobind, the long-awaited son born to Guru Arjan and Mata Ganga, sent, the hymn says, by the True Guru, who would become the sixth Guru.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: long-lived; the hymn's word for the newborn.

carryVoice: Your line: a gift arrives. Sent, the hymn says, and welcomed with song. Day six hundred fifty-six, done.
